prompt: Create ONE single image, 4:3 aspect ratio: a 2x2 grid of 4 SEPARATE illustrations (2 columns, 2 rows) for a children's picture book, all panels exactly the same size and perfectly aligned, plain white gutters between and around the panels, no frames, no captions, no text, letters or numbers anywhere. Style: Children's picture-book illustration, soft watercolor and gouache with gentle pencil lines, warm golden light, earthy palette (stone beige, olive green, terracotta, deep blue), rounded friendly faces with expressive eyes, the Land of Israel and Babylon in the time of the Mishnah and Talmud (Roman era): stone houses with flat roofs, oil lamps, study halls with low benches and scrolls, markets, olive and carob trees. Jewish sages with beards, tunics and simple robes; women in modest long dresses and head coverings. Calm, warm, safe mood. HEAD COVERING RULE for every panel: every man and every boy (including sons, shepherds, servants, neighbors and children) ALWAYS has his head covered, never bare: a kippah (skullcap) in modern or sages-era scenes, a tallit worn over the head, or in ancient scenes the hood or corner of his robe/cloak drawn over his head or a head-cloth tied with a cord. This overrides any mention of hair in a character description (the hair may show beneath the covering). Women and girls keep their head scarves or coverings as described. Keep every character exactly the same in every panel where they appear: Rabbi Elazar: young sage about 30, tall and upright, olive skin, short glossy black beard, black hair under a white head wrap, sharp dark eyes; fine long white linen robe with a deep-blue sash over a cream tunic with tzitzit corners, good leather sandals; Donkey: tall elegant light-brown donkey with a cream belly and muzzle, wearing a deep-blue saddle cloth with a simple woven border; The man: plain, ordinary-looking traveler about 45, short and broad, dark olive skin, round weathered face with a wide flat nose, heavy eyebrows, a short scruffy grey-black beard, calm wise eyes and great dignity in his posture; patched brown wool tunic, rope belt, a small cloth bundle on a stick over his shoulder; never ugly or grotesque, simply unremarkable; Townspeople: a cheerful crowd of villagers of all ages: men in beige and olive tunics with tzitzit, women in modest long dresses and head coverings in rust and blue, a few children. Panels in reading order: 1 BOOK COVER: On a riverside path at golden hour, Rabbi Elazar stands humbly with his head bowed and hands open, asking forgiveness, before the plain-looking traveler, who stands tall and dignified. Behind them, a tall slender reed bends gracefully in the breeze by the water while a big cedar stands stiff on the far bank. The donkey waits nearby. Warm, reconciling light, two-shot. 2 Rabbi Elazar rides the light-brown donkey along a calm riverbank with reeds and willows, the water flowing gently beside him in late afternoon light. He sits very upright with his chin a little high and a proud, satisfied smile. Wide landscape shot with soft reflections in the river. 3 On the riverside path, the plain-looking traveler steps aside respectfully and greets Rabbi Elazar with a warm, polite smile and a slight bow, his hand on his heart. Rabbi Elazar, still on the donkey, looks down at him. Golden afternoon light, reeds framing the scene, medium shot showing the man's kindness and dignity. 4 Rabbi Elazar, still seated high on the donkey, speaks with a haughty, dismissive gesture of his hand. The traveler below stands quietly, his smile gone, his shoulders lowered and his eyes hurt and sad. A cloud passes over the sun and the light turns a little greyer. Low angle emphasizing the gap between them, no exaggeration, the man's sadness as focus.
